newsitem.title: UK: UK money mkt rates could tighten on gilt auction.
newsitem.headline: UK money mkt rates could tighten on gilt auction.

text.p: UK money market rates were steady despite a larger than expected cash shortage but could tighten on Thursday in the wake of today's 2.5 billion stg gilt auction, dealers said.
Overnight rates were quoted at around 5-1/2 3/8 in afternoon business, little changed from yesterday's levels.
"It hasn't been a very exciting day -- a large shortage but it was taken out at lunchtime and things have been fairly comfortable after that," one trader said.
The Bank of England fully covered the forecast 1.35 billion stg shortage.
"There will be a large shortage tomorrow after the gilt auction so things could get a little tighter, but hopefully the Bank will be accommodating," the trader added.
In the gilt repo market, traders said the auction failed to provide much impetus.
"The auction has prompted selling in the cash market of other bonds such as the 6.0 percent of 1999, 8.0 of 2000 and 7.0 of 2001," one repo trader said.
"A whole host of bonds are being sold to buy the auction stock, but that has not been reflected in the repo market."

Aside from strong interest from one buyer for the 6.0s of 1999 in the one month at around 50 points through GC (general collateral) levels, traders said there were no notable factors in the repo market.
Overnight GC tracked cash rates and ranged between 4-3/4 and 6.0 percent.
